For starters, the reason that Monsanto has control over a larger percent of the GMO market is because of people like Neil Young. Monsanto, DuPont and Bayer are all large names in the GMO world and none of them focus on seeds, they tend to focus on chemicals. The reason this is important is because of the amount of time and money needed to do crop breeding.

When a business starts to do GMO research there is usually a few typical responses. The business gets boycotted, their fields get salted or their offices gets burned down. Doing GMO research is too dangerous for most small businesses in the era of radical environmental activism. The producers of GMOs are so limited exactly because of the same people that complain about how limited the market is.

I should also point out that the alternatives to GMOs are much more dangerous to small farmer's business model. Most farmers work on large yearly sums of money, assuming that they do not work elsewhere which most have to because of the limited profits. This means that small or mid sized farms are not able to switch styles of farming in any real sense. This is a financial, knowledge based and social reality. Who can switch quickly? Monsanto, DuPont and Bayer. The organic produce that you are buying at the store ain't from your local hippie. It is most likely from the same people that produced the GMO crop just on different fields.

Some people honestly do not understand how important GMOs are to the world. GMOs have revolutionized where crops can be grown, decreased overall use of pesticides, decreased loss of crops from pests and diseases. This is not to say that they are the saviors of humanity. Ignorance in farming still has drawbacks. The reason that so much cropland needs so much fertilizer is not the problem of the crop, but of farmers that do not respect the land. Crop rotation, polycultures, and water management are all good ideas, but that doesn't mean organic farming is the only solution. We need to learn overtime what works and what doesn't so we can better equip farmers to solve problems, albums that bash GMOs are counterproductive.

In my understanding of space, it doesn't warp or fold. It's just a coordinate system put on well, space.

So Black Holes pull space to what we think is a singularity... does it keep sucking in space, or just the objects in space?

Black holes don't suck in space, they just have enough gravity to keep photons from escaping it's gravity well. So you could say they keep sucking in photons. To answer your question, they will suck in object in space near enough. Not space itself. And "objects" includes photons, that's why it's not possible to see them.
